Quick update from runtime: we see a correlated increase in KV cache miss rate that started at 08:43 PDT. Misses spiked for keys associated with long sequences; this is causing more frequent decoder work and increased per-request kernel time. GPU utilization per-node is normal (no saturation), but effective throughput dropped because more tokens are being recomputed.

Hypothesis: a cache invalidation event or a subtle regression in prefix-hash bucketization increased cache fragmentation overnight. Not seeing new deploys, so likely data-driven (different workload pattern) or a cached-index corruption.

Immediate mitigations attempted (09:40–09:50):
- Increased batch time window to accept slightly larger batches (reduced P50 but increased P95 in short term) — reverted.
- Forced warming of hot prefixes on a subset of pools — preliminary improvement in P95 (~2.1s) for test traffic.

Next steps: collect KV cache diagnostics, run a targeted re-warm of top-10 prefixes for affected pools, and consider temporary routing of Acme traffic to warmed pools / fallback variant with smaller KV footprint.

—Markus
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
